The paper does not specify tokenizer special-token behavior, padding values, attention masks, loss masks, or sequence-boundary handling during packed pretraining inputs.
The paper does not provide the exact decoder input/label shift used for causal language-model training.
The paper does not document the internal Transformer computation that converts token IDs to hidden states or next-token distributions.
The paper does not specify whether optional species and gene fields are represented by omission, empty fields, or special tokens.
The paper does not provide the exact implementation of softmax, repetition penalties, no-repeat n-gram filtering, or termination handling beyond the stated decoding description.
The paper does not document the exact extraction and translation implementation used for generated CDS evaluation; those procedures are downstream validation rather than model-input construction.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The paper explicitly describes parsing GenBank records and extracting molecule type, species, gene name, and functional descriptions, but the catalog has no operation for structured-record parsing or field extraction.

The catalog represents attention primitives but has no operation for the complete decoder-only Transformer stack with causal masking and next-token distribution output. The paper does not expose an operation-level decomposition of that stack.

operation_proposals.why_no_existing_operation: The catalog can represent exclusion of padding with selection, but it has no mean-pooling operation whose output is the fixed-dimensional average described in the paper.

evidence.quote: We used Biopython to parse GenBank records automatically. For each valid record, we extracted the molecule type (genomic DNA or RNA), source species, gene name, and natural-language functional descriptions from the product and note fields.

For hierarchical structures such as mRNA, CDS, ncRNA, and regulatory elements, we organized the annotations using custom XML-style tags so as to preserve the original structural boundaries and semantic cues as much as possible, and wrote these structured annotations together with the corresponding underlying nucleotide sequences into unified training samples.
During unsupervised BPE merging, high-frequency co-occurrence patterns from different modalities were mapped into a shared token space.

To improve context utilization and GPU memory efficiency during Transformer pretraining, we further applied a sequence-packing strategy during preprocessing, concatenating multiple samples into long input sequences of nearly 20,000 characters.
During construction of training inputs, the species identifier or gene identifier in the prompt was randomly removed with probability 0.5.
